instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
passage:
On Monday morning, Leila arrives at a small community workshop where people mend donated furniture. A supervisor named Omar begins the day with a short safety meeting. He asks everyone to look for a hazard before starting. A hazard is something that could cause harm, while a risk describes the chance of harm. Omar uses a simple example: water on the floor is a danger because someone could slip. The team agrees that it is better to prevent a problem than to wait for an accident.

Leila is carrying a light chair toward a table when she notices a spill beside the door. The floor is slippery there. She stops and gives a signal to the people behind her. Her signal is to raise one hand and point toward the wet area. She does not try to carry the chair across it. Instead, she puts the chair down and tells Omar what she saw. He asks the group to use caution and take a different path while he checks the area.

Omar places a bright barrier around the spill. He keeps the exit clear because a box must never block a way out. Another worker finds a cloth. Omar checks that each glove is dry and puts on a clean pair before cleaning the small area. The team does not need to touch any unknown liquid in this fictional example; it is water from a dropped cup. Once the floor is dry, Omar asks Leila to inspect it with him. They agree that the path is safe to use again.

Later, two people prepare to move a heavy cabinet. They discuss how to avoid straining a shoulder or the back. Omar explains that the group should stop and ask for help whenever an item is too heavy to move comfortably. They decide to push the cabinet together across a short, clear path rather than pull it through a narrow space. Leila walks beside it so that she can watch the corners. The movers check their balance and make sure the path stays clear. They do not try to balance the cabinet on a small ladder, because it could fall.

At the end of the morning, Omar asks the team to describe what happened. Leila says that she was walking toward the table when she saw the water. Another worker was opening a window while Omar was putting up the barrier. No one was hurt, and there was no serious damage. The group writes a brief note so that the next team knows to keep drinks away from the work area. At their next meeting they will ask whether a separate place for cups would help; they know that one conversation cannot solve every problem. They also check where the alarm and the exit are. The story is a language exercise; it does not replace the workshop's own safety instructions.
